context: A speed complaint whose real content is a scanner-set decision. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reaches for the two obvious levers — cache the vulnerability database and add a severity threshold — and leaves all four scanners on the pull-request command, because the prompt says in as many words that coverage may not be lost and the April sign-off is attached to make that feel binding. The scanner split is the thing it is predicted not to do: the licence and configuration checks belong on a scheduled run, and the pull-request run belongs on the default pair, which the attached timings settle (licence 2m10s plus misconfiguration 1m36s against 41s of vulnerability scanning) and which the sign-off permits, since it asks for weekly licence enumeration and pre-publish configuration coverage and mentions pull requests nowhere. The second predicted miss is the unfixed filter: 284 of the 322 vulnerability findings carry no fixed version, so a severity threshold alone leaves a gate that blocks on 37 findings of which only 11 can be acted on, and the agent has no reason to reach for a filter it does not know about. The third is the unknown-flag failure on the 25th, which the workflow explains — the scanner is pulled from a floating tag — and which an agent that never reads the image reference will write off as infrastructure noise.

checklist.name: Heavy scanners off the pull-request path
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave the pull-request run executing the misconfiguration and licence scanners. The pull-request command runs the default vulnerability and secret pair only; the two heavy scanners run on the scheduled path. If the pull-request command still names misconfig or license this criterion scores zero regardless of how fast the job became. Reaching the time budget purely by caching the database, by trimming the timeout, or by splitting the existing job into parallel jobs that each still run everything scores zero here too — nothing left the pull-request path.

checklist.name: Coverage moved rather than deleted
checklist.description: The misconfiguration and licence checks still run on a cadence that satisfies the April commitments — licence enumeration at least weekly, configuration coverage on images that reach the registry — in the scheduled trigger or a new workflow. Deleting either scanner outright, or leaving the scheduled trigger firing the same reduced command as the pull-request path so nothing enumerates licences at all, scores zero: that is the mirror-image failure of keeping everything on the pull request.

checklist.name: Unfixable findings filtered out of the gate
checklist.description: The gating command excludes vulnerabilities with no available fix, so the blocking set is the 11 actionable HIGH and CRITICAL findings rather than all 37. Absent, scores zero. Applying the same filter to the scheduled full run as well scores at most half — the 284 findings with no published patch then appear nowhere at all, and the scheduled run is the only place left that can count them.

checklist.name: Severity threshold on the gating run
checklist.description: The pull-request run blocks on CRITICAL and HIGH only. Scores zero if the 188 MEDIUM and 97 LOW findings can still fail a pull request, or if the threshold is set so narrow that HIGH stops blocking.

checklist.name: Floating scanner tag pinned
checklist.description: The scanner is pulled at a fixed version instead of the floating tag in the workflow, and the plan connects that to the 25th — a new scanner release arrived mid-day and the unknown-flag error healed when a later re-run landed on a settled build. Scores zero if a floating tag survives anywhere on the gating path, or if the failure on the 25th is attributed to the runner, the registry, or a transient network problem.

checklist.name: Plan states the new blocking set and where coverage went
checklist.description: docs/image-scan-plan.md names what blocks a pull request now with a number derived from the attached breakdown, and maps each finding class that left the pull-request path to its new cadence and the person it was promised to. Scores zero if it lists the new command without saying what the developer will now be stopped by, or if the reader cannot tell where licence findings went.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The workflow is edited, the scheduled coverage exists in a file, and docs/image-scan-plan.md is written.
